title: AWS Cloud Practitioner (CLF-C02) practice exam
note: Original questions written for MyNextCert from AWS's public CLF-C02 exam guide (domains, weights and task statements; https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-certification/latest/cloud-practitioner-02/cloud-practitioner-02.html), checked 2026-11-26. Not real exam questions. The real exam has 65 questions (50 scored and 15 unscored) in 90 minutes with no hands-on items. This bank is a 60-item stand-in that fits 90 minutes, follows the 24/30/34/12 domain weights, and adds 4 hands-on items (AWS CLI, CloudTrail log, account lockdown order, VPC layout; each exam draws 3) plus a few choose-two items like the real exam.

q.q: A unit's web portal sees ten times its normal traffic for one week each year during open enrollment, then drops back. Which cloud benefit best fits this pattern?
o: Elasticity: capacity grows, then shrinks
Right. Elasticity means resources scale out and back in with demand, so you pay for the peak only while it lasts.
Buying hardware sized for the busiest week
That is the on-premises habit. The hardware sits idle the other fifty-one weeks.
A fixed monthly price whatever the usage
Most AWS services bill by use. A flat price would not follow the spikes.
Moving the portal to a single large server
One big server is still a fixed size. It cannot grow past its limit or shrink when traffic falls.

q.q: A team needs a test environment in another country by Friday. On premises, this would mean ordering and shipping hardware. Which AWS cloud advantage does this describe?
o: Lower prices from your own purchasing power
Economies of scale are AWS's, from its huge size. They lower per-unit prices but do not cover the speed of deploying abroad.
Global reach by using another Region
Right. AWS Regions around the world let you deploy close to users with a few clicks or one template, with no shipping.
Guaranteed zero downtime for every resource
AWS offers high availability tools, but you still design for failure. Nothing is guaranteed zero downtime.
Owning the hardware in the new country
With AWS you do not own the hardware. That is the point of the model.

q.q: Which statement describes the benefit of massive economies of scale in the AWS Cloud?
o: Each customer usually gets a private data center
Most services run on shared infrastructure. Private hardware costs extra, as with Dedicated Hosts.
Customers need a three-year contract for price cuts
Pay-as-you-go needs no contract. Commitments such as Savings Plans are optional extras.
AWS buys at huge volume and passes on lower prices
Right. AWS buys hardware and runs data centers at huge volume, and passes part of that saving to customers.
AWS takes over securing the customer's data
Security is still shared. You protect your own data and access.

q.q: Which TWO items are benefits of the AWS Cloud? (Choose two.)
o: Pay for a full data center even when it is idle
That is how on-premises works. The cloud lets you stop paying when you stop using.
Stop guessing capacity: scale up or down as needs change
Right. You no longer buy hardware based on a forecast that might be wrong.
Wait several weeks for hardware to arrive
Resources launch in minutes, which is a core benefit.
Trade fixed expenses for variable expenses
Right. Instead of large up-front purchases, you pay for what you use, when you use it.
Keep full responsibility for the physical buildings
AWS owns and secures the facilities under the shared responsibility model.

q.q: A review team asks whether the workload can recover from a failed Availability Zone and still meet its targets. Which Well-Architected pillar is being checked?
o: Cost optimization
This pillar looks at avoiding unneeded spending, not recovery from failures.
Sustainability
This pillar covers reducing the environmental impact of running workloads.
Performance efficiency
This pillar is about choosing the right resource types and sizes for the job.
Reliability
Right. Reliability is the ability to recover from failures and meet demand, such as surviving the loss of a zone.

q.q: A company moves a batch job to smaller instances during off hours and shuts down test servers at night to avoid paying for idle capacity. Which pillar does this follow?
o: Cost optimization
Right. Matching capacity to need and switching off waste is the heart of cost optimization.
Security
The security pillar is about protecting data and systems, not trimming spend.
Operational excellence
That pillar is about running, monitoring and improving operations. Saving money is not its main aim.
Reliability
Shutting off test servers does nothing for recovery or availability.

q.q: Which design principle in the Well-Architected Framework is applied when you enable encryption, grant least privilege and trace every action?
o: Performance efficiency pillar
This pillar concerns using computing resources efficiently as needs change.
Security pillar
Right. Protecting data, managing identities and keeping traceability are all in the security pillar.
Sustainability pillar
This pillar focuses on reducing environmental impact.
Operational excellence pillar
It covers running and improving workloads, not protecting data or identities.

q.q: Which TWO choices are among the six pillars of the AWS Well-Architected Framework? (Choose two.)
o: Compliance
Compliance is a goal supported by the pillars, but it is not one of the six.
Performance efficiency
Right. It covers selecting the right resources and keeping them effective as demand shifts.
Scalability
Scalability is a property that the pillars help you achieve. It is not a pillar by itself.
Profitability
Profit is a business result, not a pillar.
Sustainability
Right. Sustainability was added as the sixth pillar to cover environmental impact.

q.q: A group wants guidance on how its business, people, governance and security teams should prepare for moving to AWS. Which resource organizes this advice into perspectives?
o: AWS Well-Architected Tool
It reviews a specific workload against the pillars. It does not plan organization-wide adoption.
AWS Trusted Advisor
It checks your account for cost, security and performance recommendations.
AWS Cloud Adoption Framework (AWS CAF)
Right. The CAF groups guidance into perspectives such as business, people, governance, platform, security and operations.
AWS Artifact
It provides AWS compliance reports and agreements.

q.q: Eight hundred terabytes must reach AWS from a site with a very slow Internet link, and it cannot wait months. Which option fits?
o: Copy it over the Internet with a single script
At a slow link speed this would take far too long.
Amazon CloudFront
CloudFront delivers content to users quickly. It is not a bulk import tool.
AWS Shield
Shield defends against DDoS attacks, which has nothing to do with moving data.
Snowball Edge devices shipped both ways
Right. Snow Family devices carry data physically, which beats a slow link for very large transfers.

q.q: A team moves its database from a self-managed server to Amazon RDS but keeps the application as it is. Which migration strategy is this?
o: Replatform
Right. Replatforming makes a few cloud changes, such as using a managed database, without redesigning the app.
Rehost
Rehost moves the system with no changes at all, including its database.
Retire
Retire switches off an application you no longer need.
Refactor
Refactor rebuilds the application, for example into serverless functions. That goes well beyond swapping the database.

q.q: A unit's lawyers want to know why moving to the cloud often lowers total cost of ownership. Which on-premises costs go away or shrink?
o: Software licenses that you bring with you
Bring-your-own-license costs stay with you. AWS does not cover them.
Space, power, cooling and hardware refresh
Right. AWS carries these costs, so the customer no longer budgets for them directly.
Salaries for the staff who manage user access
Identity and access management stays your job.
Fees to move data out of AWS
Data transfer out is a cost that on-premises networks did not have in the same form.

q.q: Which choice shows how a managed service lowers cloud costs for a team that has no database administrator?
o: Installing the database engine on an EC2 instance
This gives you control but leaves patches and backups to your team.
Buying a larger server to be safe
Oversizing adds cost. Right-sizing is the cost-saving habit.
RDS handles patching and backups for the team
Right. Managed services take over routine work, which saves staff time and lowers the cost of running the database.
Keeping the database in a closet server room
Local hardware brings power, cooling and refresh costs.

q.q: A review finds that a production server uses 8% of its CPU and memory every day. Which action best reduces cost without hurting the workload?
o: Move to a larger instance type for headroom
A larger size costs more and the data shows it is not needed.
Stop using monitoring to save on fees
Without monitoring you cannot right-size at all.
Buy a three-year commitment for the current size
Committing to an oversized instance locks in waste.
Right-size to a smaller instance type
Right. Matching size to measured use cuts the bill. You can scale back up if needs grow.

q.q: Under the shared responsibility model, which task belongs to AWS for an Amazon EC2 instance?
o: Securing the data center and its network
Right. Security OF the cloud, meaning facilities, hardware and core network, is always AWS's job.
Installing operating system patches
On EC2 the guest operating system is the customer's job.
Choosing which ports the security group opens
Firewall rules for your instances are set by you.
Deciding who can read the data you store
Data classification and access are the customer's responsibility.

q.q: A customer runs an app on AWS Lambda. Compared with EC2, which duty has moved from the customer to AWS?
o: Writing secure application code
Your code is still yours to secure.
Maintaining the servers under the code
Right. With Lambda, AWS manages the servers and the platform under your code.
Managing IAM permissions for the function
Permissions for who and what can invoke or be reached remain with the customer.
Encrypting your own data
Deciding how your data is protected is shared with you, not moved away.

q.q: Which TWO responsibilities belong to the customer when using Amazon S3? (Choose two.)
o: Maintaining the storage hardware
AWS owns and replaces the hardware.
Protecting the data center with guards and cameras
Physical security is AWS's responsibility.
Setting bucket policies and access permissions
Right. Controlling who can read or write the bucket is a customer duty.
Patching the S3 service software
AWS runs and patches the service itself.
Choosing whether to encrypt objects and managing the keys used
Right. Customers decide how their data is encrypted. S3 gives the options.

q.q: Which statement about the shared responsibility model is correct?
o: AWS handles nearly everything inside customer accounts
Customers remain responsible for their data, identities and settings.
The customer is responsible for AWS's data centers
Facilities are AWS's.
The split of duties changes depending on the AWS service used
Right. For example, the customer handles more with EC2 and less with a managed service like DynamoDB.
It applies mainly to government customers
The model applies to every AWS customer.

q.q: An auditor asks for evidence that AWS data centers meet a recognized standard. Where does the unit download AWS's own audit reports?
o: AWS Config
Config records how your own resources are configured over time.
Amazon Inspector
Inspector scans your workloads for software flaws.
AWS CloudFormation
CloudFormation builds resources from templates. It holds no reports.
AWS Artifact
Right. Artifact is the portal for AWS's compliance reports and agreements.

q.q: Security needs a record of who called which API in an account, including from the console and the CLI. Which service provides this?
o: AWS CloudTrail
Right. CloudTrail logs account activity and API calls, which gives you an audit trail.
Amazon CloudWatch
CloudWatch collects metrics and logs for performance and alarms. The API history comes from CloudTrail.
AWS Shield
Shield protects against DDoS attacks.
Amazon Route 53
Route 53 is DNS and does not track account actions.

q.q: A team must show every month that its resources still match required settings, such as encrypted volumes, and see when one changes. Which service records and evaluates resource configurations?
o: Amazon GuardDuty
GuardDuty detects suspicious activity. It is not a configuration tracker.
AWS Config
Right. Config tracks configuration history and can check it against rules.
AWS Direct Connect
Direct Connect is a private network link.
Amazon SNS
SNS sends notifications and does not record configurations.

q.q: Which TWO methods protect data in transit on AWS? (Choose two.)
o: Turning on server-side encryption of an S3 bucket
This protects data at rest, once it is stored.
Enabling EBS encryption
That is encryption at rest for volumes.
Using TLS for connections to services
Right. TLS encrypts data as it moves between client and service.
Creating a backup of a database
A backup helps recovery. It does not encrypt traffic.
Using an IPsec VPN to connect an office to a VPC
Right. A VPN tunnel encrypts traffic across the Internet.

q.q: What is the best practice for the AWS account root user after the account is created?
o: Share its password with the whole admin team
Sharing destroys accountability and raises the risk of misuse.
Create access keys for it and put them in scripts
Root access keys should never exist. They can do everything.
Turn on MFA, then avoid using it for daily tasks
Right. The root user has unlimited power, so protect it with MFA and use other identities for work.
Give it to a vendor for safekeeping
This hands the keys of the account to someone else.

q.q: A new analyst needs read-only access to a few S3 buckets and nothing else. Which principle should guide the permissions?
o: Administrator access, so nothing is blocked
Full access gives a mistake or stolen login the widest possible reach.
Shared credentials for the whole team
Shared logins make actions untraceable to a person.
Public access to the buckets
Public buckets expose data to everyone.
Least privilege, granting only the access needed
Right. Give the smallest set of permissions that lets the person do the job.

q.q: An app running on an EC2 instance needs to call the DynamoDB service. What is the most secure way to give it access?
o: Attach an IAM role to the instance
Right. Roles supply temporary credentials that rotate automatically, so there is no long-lived key.
Store an IAM user's access key in the application code
Keys in code get copied, committed to repositories and leaked.
Use the root user's credentials
Root should never be used by an application.
Open the table to the public
This exposes the data to the whole Internet.

q.q: A department with many AWS accounts wants staff to sign in once with their existing directory credentials and reach their accounts. Which service fits?
o: AWS Secrets Manager
It stores and rotates secrets like database passwords. It does not sign people in.
AWS IAM Identity Center
Right. IAM Identity Center provides single sign-on across accounts and applications.
AWS WAF
WAF filters web requests and does not manage logins.
Amazon Inspector
Inspector scans for software vulnerabilities.

q.q: Which TWO actions strengthen the security of IAM users? (Choose two.)
o: Attach the AdministratorAccess policy to every user
This gives everyone too much power.
Write the access keys in a shared document
A shared document leaks easily.
Require multi-factor authentication
Right. A second factor blocks most logins that use only a stolen password.
Reuse one password across all accounts
One leak then opens every account.
Rotate access keys on a schedule and remove those unused
Right. Old or unused keys are a common way in.

q.q: A web application is being hit by SQL injection and cross-site scripting attempts. Which AWS service filters these requests at the application layer?
o: Amazon Macie
Macie finds sensitive data in S3.
AWS Artifact
Artifact is a library of compliance documents.
AWS WAF
Right. WAF inspects web requests and blocks common attack patterns with rules you set.
Amazon Inspector
Inspector scans for vulnerabilities, but it does not filter live web traffic.

q.q: A video site is flooded with traffic from thousands of sources and users cannot connect. Which service is built to protect against this type of attack?
o: AWS Config
Config tracks configuration changes.
AWS KMS
KMS manages encryption keys.
Amazon Cognito
Cognito handles sign-in for app users.
AWS Shield
Right. Shield defends applications against distributed denial of service attacks.

q.q: Which service continuously analyzes CloudTrail events, VPC flow logs and DNS logs to find threats such as a compromised instance?
o: Amazon GuardDuty
Right. GuardDuty is a managed threat detection service that needs no agents to install.
Amazon Inspector
Inspector looks for software vulnerabilities, not live threat activity.
AWS Trusted Advisor
It gives account best-practice checks.
AWS Artifact
It provides compliance reports.

q.q: Which statement describes a security group in a VPC?
o: A stateless filter applied to a whole subnet
That describes a network ACL.
A stateful firewall at the instance level that allows traffic by rule
Right. Security groups are stateful and only allow traffic. Return traffic is permitted automatically.
A service that scans instances for flaws
That is Amazon Inspector.
A rule set that blocks Internet attacks in front of CloudFront
That is AWS WAF or Shield.

q.q: A security officer wants one place to see findings from GuardDuty, Inspector and other services, with checks against security standards. Which service does this?
o: AWS Direct Connect
Direct Connect provides a private network connection.
Amazon SQS
SQS is a message queue.
AWS Security Hub
Right. Security Hub gathers findings and runs automated checks against standards.
AWS Snowball
Snowball is for moving large data offline.

q.q: A team wants to build the same set of servers and networks in three accounts from one text file that can be reviewed and reused. Which service fits?
o: AWS Direct Connect
This is a private network link, not a deployment tool.
Amazon Route 53
Route 53 is DNS and domain registration.
AWS Snowcone
A Snowcone is a small physical data-transfer device.
AWS CloudFormation
Right. CloudFormation provisions resources from templates, which is infrastructure as code.

q.q: An office needs a private, dedicated connection to AWS that does not travel over the public Internet. Which option provides it?
o: AWS Direct Connect
Right. Direct Connect is a dedicated network link from your site to AWS.
AWS Site-to-Site VPN
A VPN encrypts traffic but still goes over the public Internet.
Amazon CloudFront
CloudFront caches content near users.
Internet gateway
An Internet gateway links a VPC to the Internet, which is public by nature.

q.q: Which way of working with AWS lets an engineer run repeatable tasks from a terminal or script?
o: The console's graphical pages only
Clicking works for one-off tasks but is hard to repeat the same way.
The AWS Command Line Interface (CLI)
Right. The CLI turns commands into scripts that can be repeated and checked.
AWS Artifact reports
Artifact holds documents, not a way to run tasks.
A support case
Support helps with problems and does not run your tasks.

q.q: A company must keep customer data in a specific country because of the law. Which choice lets it control this?
o: Selecting an edge location in that country
Edge locations cache content. They do not hold the primary copy of your data.
Using more Availability Zones
AZs add resilience within one Region. They do not pick a country.
Selecting an AWS Region in that country
Right. Data stays in the Region you choose unless you move it.
Using a larger instance size
Size has no link to where data lives.

q.q: A company wants an application to survive the failure of a whole data center. Which design does this?
o: Place all instances in a single Availability Zone
One zone is one failure domain.
Use only one large instance
A single server is a single point of failure.
Back up to the same server
A backup on the failed server is lost too.
Spread instances across two or more Availability Zones
Right. AZs are separate data centers, so one failing does not take down the rest.

q.q: What does Amazon CloudFront use edge locations for?
o: Caching content near viewers
Right. Edge locations store copies of content near viewers so pages load faster.
Running the primary database for an app
Databases run in Regions, not at the edge.
Replacing Availability Zones
They have different roles. Edge locations do not host your main workloads.
Holding compliance reports
Those are in AWS Artifact.

q.q: A web store needs the number of servers to grow when traffic rises and shrink when it falls, without staff action. Which service does this?
o: Elastic Load Balancing
A load balancer spreads traffic but does not add or remove instances by itself.
Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling
Right. Auto Scaling adds and removes instances based on rules you set.
Amazon S3 Glacier
This is archive storage.
AWS Direct Connect
This is a network link.

q.q: A developer wants to run code in response to a file upload and pay only while the code runs, with no servers to manage. Which service fits?
o: Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances
Reserved capacity bills whether or not it is used and still means managing servers.
Amazon Lightsail
Lightsail gives simple virtual servers that you manage.
AWS Lambda
Right. Lambda is serverless compute billed by the time your code runs.
AWS Elastic Beanstalk
Beanstalk deploys apps on managed instances. You still pay for those instances all the time.

q.q: Which TWO services run containers on AWS? (Choose two.)
o: Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS)
Right. ECS is AWS's own container orchestration service.
Amazon Redshift
Redshift is a data warehouse.
Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS)
Right. EKS runs Kubernetes on AWS.
Amazon Athena
Athena queries data in S3 with SQL.
AWS Artifact
Artifact is a compliance portal.

q.q: A unit wants a relational database without managing the operating system or taking backups by hand. Which service fits?
o: MySQL installed on an EC2 instance
This works but leaves patches and backups to your team.
Amazon S3
S3 is object storage, not a relational database.
Amazon ElastiCache
ElastiCache is an in-memory cache and not a main relational store.
Amazon RDS
Right. RDS is a managed relational database that handles patching and automatic backups.

q.q: An online game needs a key-value database with single-digit millisecond response at any scale and no servers to manage. Which service fits?
o: Amazon DynamoDB
Right. DynamoDB is a serverless NoSQL database built for fast key-value access.
Amazon Redshift
Redshift is for analytics on large data sets.
Amazon RDS for Oracle
A relational database that you size and scale.
Amazon Neptune
A graph database for connected data.

q.q: A social app must store and query relationships such as who follows whom. Which database type is designed for this?
o: A data warehouse such as Amazon Redshift
Warehouses are designed for reporting across large tables.
A graph database such as Amazon Neptune
Right. Graph databases are built to follow relationships between items.
An in-memory cache such as Amazon ElastiCache
Caches speed up reads. They are not a relationship store.
Object storage such as Amazon S3
S3 holds files, not linked records.

q.q: Which component directs traffic out of a private subnet to the Internet for updates, but blocks connections started from the Internet?
o: A route to an Internet gateway in the private subnet
With a route to an Internet gateway the subnet is public, and inbound access would be possible.
A second VPC peering link
Peering joins VPCs. It does not give Internet access.
A NAT gateway
Right. A NAT gateway lets private instances start outbound connections only.
AWS Shield
Shield defends against DDoS and does not route traffic.

q.q: Which service provides DNS and can route users to the healthiest or closest endpoint?
o: AWS Global Accelerator
Global Accelerator improves routing over the AWS network by static IP addresses. It is not DNS.
AWS Direct Connect
This is a dedicated network link.
Amazon VPC
A VPC is your private network. It is not a DNS service.
Amazon Route 53
Right. Route 53 is AWS's DNS service with health checks and routing policies.

q.q: What is the main difference between a network ACL and a security group?
o: A network ACL is stateless and works at the subnet level
Right. NACLs check each direction separately and can allow or deny.
A network ACL is stateful and works on a single instance
That reverses the two. Security groups are stateful.
A security group can write explicit deny rules
Security groups only have allow rules.
Both are the same thing
They are two layers with different scope and behavior.

q.q: A company stores records for seven years. They are almost never read, and a retrieval time of several hours is fine. Which S3 storage class is the cheapest fit?
o: S3 Standard
Standard is for frequent access and costs more to hold.
S3 Glacier Deep Archive
Right. Deep Archive is the lowest-cost class for data kept long and rarely accessed.
S3 Intelligent-Tiering
It moves objects by access pattern. Archive classes are cheaper for known cold data.
Amazon EBS
EBS is a block volume for an EC2 instance.

q.q: Linux servers in several Availability Zones must mount the same shared file system at once. Which service fits?
o: Amazon EBS
An EBS volume sits in one AZ and normally attaches to one instance.
Amazon S3 Glacier
This is archive storage.
Amazon EFS
Right. EFS is a shared, elastic file system that many instances can use together.
Instance store
It belongs to one host and is lost when the instance stops.

q.q: A team wants S3 to move objects to a cheaper class after 90 days and delete them after a year, with no manual work. Which feature does this?
o: S3 Transfer Acceleration
It speeds uploads from far away. It does not manage age rules.
S3 Object Lock
It prevents deletion for a period. It does not move or expire data.
S3 bucket policy
A policy controls who can access the bucket.
S3 Lifecycle rules
Right. Lifecycle rules change storage class or delete objects on a schedule.

q.q: A researcher wants to run SQL queries directly on files stored in S3 without loading them into a database or managing servers. Which service fits?
o: Amazon Athena
Right. Athena is a serverless query service for data in S3.
Amazon RDS
RDS is a database service. You would first load the data.
Amazon EMR
EMR runs big data clusters that you set up.
Amazon Lex
Lex builds chatbots.

q.q: A call center wants to turn recorded phone calls into written text. Which AI service does this?
o: Amazon Polly
Polly does the reverse: it turns text into speech.
Amazon Transcribe
Right. Transcribe converts speech to text.
Amazon Rekognition
Rekognition analyzes images and video.
Amazon Comprehend
Comprehend analyzes text for meaning, such as sentiment. It does not transcribe audio.

q.q: Which service helps a team build interactive dashboards and charts to share business data across the organization?
o: AWS Glue
Glue prepares and moves data, with no dashboards.
Amazon Kinesis
Kinesis handles streaming data.
Amazon QuickSight
Right. QuickSight is AWS's business intelligence and dashboard service.
Amazon Textract
Textract pulls text and fields out of scanned documents.

q.q: An order system needs to decouple the website from the processing step so orders are held in a queue until a worker is ready. Which service fits?
o: Amazon SNS
SNS pushes a message to many subscribers at once. It is not a holding queue.
Amazon CloudWatch
CloudWatch monitors metrics and logs.
AWS CodeBuild
CodeBuild compiles and tests code.
Amazon SQS
Right. SQS is a managed message queue that holds messages until they are processed.

q.q: Employees need secure virtual desktops that they can reach from any device without buying new PCs. Which service provides this?
o: Amazon WorkSpaces
Right. WorkSpaces is a managed desktop-as-a-service offering.
Amazon Connect
Connect is a cloud contact center.
AWS Amplify
Amplify builds web and mobile front ends.
AWS IoT Core
IoT Core links connected devices.

q.q: Which TWO services support a software delivery pipeline on AWS? (Choose two.)
o: AWS CodePipeline
Right. CodePipeline automates the steps from code change to release.
Amazon Polly
Polly turns text into speech.
AWS CodeBuild
Right. CodeBuild compiles source code and runs tests.
Amazon Neptune
Neptune is a graph database.
AWS Shield
Shield protects against DDoS attacks.

q.q: A workload must run steadily for the next three years on a known instance family. Which pricing option lowers cost the most for that pattern?
o: On-Demand Instances
On-Demand has no commitment but the highest rate for a steady workload.
Savings Plans
Right. Committing for one or three years in return for a lower hourly rate suits steady use.
Spot Instances
Spot is cheap but AWS can take the capacity back, which is risky for steady work.
Dedicated Hosts only
These are for license or compliance needs and usually cost more.

q.q: A research job can be stopped and restarted at any time without harm. Which EC2 option usually costs the least?
o: On-Demand Instances
They cost more and the job does not need the guarantee.
Dedicated Hosts
These cost the most and fit license rules.
Spot Instances
Right. Spot uses spare capacity at a deep discount, with the risk of interruption.
Reserved Instances
They need a commitment for a job that may stop soon.

q.q: Which charge is generally NOT billed by AWS for typical use?
o: Data transferred out of AWS to the Internet
Outbound data is billed by the gigabyte.
Storage kept in an S3 bucket
S3 charges for the storage used.
Compute running on EC2
EC2 is billed for the time instances run.
Data transferred into AWS from the Internet
Right. Inbound data transfer is generally free.

q.q: A manager wants an email when monthly spend is forecast to pass $500. Which service sets this up?
o: AWS Budgets
Right. Budgets lets you set cost limits and sends alerts when actual or forecast spend crosses them.
AWS Artifact
Artifact is for compliance documents.
AWS Trusted Advisor
It makes recommendations and does not track a spending limit like this.
Amazon Inspector
It scans for software flaws.

q.q: A finance team wants to see last quarter's spend by service and spot trends in a chart. Which tool fits?
o: AWS Pricing Calculator
The calculator estimates future cost for planned resources. It does not show past spending.
AWS Cost Explorer
Right. Cost Explorer shows and forecasts costs and usage over time.
AWS Config
Config tracks configuration changes.
AWS Health Dashboard
It reports service events that may affect you.

q.q: A department with ten AWS accounts wants one bill and combined volume discounts. Which feature gives this?
o: Cost allocation tags
Tags label resources for reports. They do not merge bills.
AWS Support Business plan
A support plan has no link to how accounts are billed.
Consolidated billing
Right. One payer account receives a single bill and usage is combined for pricing tiers.
Amazon CloudWatch alarms
Alarms watch metrics rather than merge bills.

q.q: Which AWS Support plan feature includes access to a designated technical account manager?
o: The Basic plan
Basic gives only documentation, forums and core checks.
The Developer plan
Developer supports business hours email for testing and early work.
Most plans include one at no extra cost
Higher plans cost more, and the Basic plan is free. Only the top plans include a manager.
The Enterprise plan
Right. A technical account manager comes with the top plans such as Enterprise.

q.q: A team wants to see recommendations about cost, performance, security and fault tolerance for its account. Which service gives them?
o: AWS Trusted Advisor
Right. Trusted Advisor checks your account against best practices in these areas.
AWS Artifact
Artifact is a document library.
AWS Direct Connect
This is a network link.
Amazon Route 53
This is DNS.

q.q: Where can a unit find a community-driven place to ask technical questions and read answers from AWS experts and other users?

q.title: Find out why a bucket may be public
q.scenario: A teammate says a bucket with payroll exports might be readable by anyone. You work in the unit's own AWS account, and the account owner approved a review of this one bucket in writing. Use the AWS CLI to see what is there, find out why it is open, then close the exposure without deleting anything.
q.ticket: CHG-2207: review bucket unit-hr-exports only. Do not delete, copy or download any files. Other buckets are out of scope.
q.intro: AWS CloudShell, signed in as review-admin. Your folder holds block.json, a file with all four Block Public Access settings set to true. Type a command.

cmds.out: An error occurred (NoSuchPublicAccessBlockConfiguration) when calling the GetPublicAccessBlock operation: The public access block configuration was not found
(no output: the bucket's public access block is now on)
Not run: deleting the bucket or its files destroys the data and the evidence of what was exposed. Close the exposure and report it instead.
Not run: the ticket says do not copy or download files. Pulling payroll data into a shell spreads sensitive data that you do not need to read.
Not run: only unit-hr-exports is in scope for this change.

checks.t: Listed the buckets to find the one named in the ticket
checks.why: aws s3 ls shows the account's buckets. It confirms the bucket exists before you inspect it.

checks.t: Found that no public access block protects the bucket
checks.why: The error means the bucket has no Block Public Access settings, so nothing stops a public policy from taking effect.

checks.t: Found the policy that lets everyone read the files
checks.why: The policy allows Principal * to run s3:GetObject. That means anyone on the Internet can download the exports.

checks.t: Turned on Block Public Access for the bucket
checks.why: Block Public Access overrides public policies and ACLs, so it closes the exposure while keeping the data. The policy can then be reviewed and removed by the owner.

checks.t: Did not delete the bucket or its files
checks.why: The files belong to the unit and may be evidence. Closing access fixes the problem and keeps both.

checks.t: Stayed in scope: no downloads and no other buckets
checks.why: The ticket named one bucket and said not to copy files. Staying inside written approval is the rule for any review.

q.title: Read the account's CloudTrail events
q.scenario: GuardDuty flagged an access key belonging to the deploy user svc-deploy. You are authorized to review the account's own CloudTrail log for the night. Mark every event that belongs to the attack, then say what happened.
q.ticket: Finding GD-5521: svc-deploy key used from an unusual address. Review events from 01:50 to 11:10.

lines.why: A staff member signs in with MFA from the unit network. This is routine.
The deploy key is used from an outside address with a scripting tool. Attackers often start by asking who the key belongs to.
The same outside address now maps out what data exists. Pipelines do not browse the bucket list.

lines.text: 02:13:22 CreateUser userName=backup-svc2 by svc-deploy src=198.51.100.23 src=198.51.100.23
lines.why: A deploy key has no reason to create people or accounts. This is a new way back in.

lines.text: 02:13:58 AttachUserPolicy user=backup-svc2 policy=AdministratorAccess by svc-deploy src=198.51.100.23
lines.why: The new account gets full control. That is privilege escalation.
A long-lived key for the new admin gives the attacker steady access even if svc-deploy is fixed.
Switching off the audit trail hides later actions. It is a defense-evasion step.
The scheduled backup service starts at its normal time with its own role.
The pipeline launches a small test server from the unit network at work hours. This matches its job.
A normal upload by a staff member from the unit network.
An audit role reads instance data from the security team's address, which is routine.

ask.label: What does this log show?
opts: A stolen deploy key used from outside, then an admin made
A normal night of pipeline jobs and a staff login
A backup job that retried and created a backup user
A failed attack in which nothing was changed
ask.why: One outside address used the deploy key, then created an admin user and key and stopped CloudTrail. The other events are staff and scheduled jobs. The new user and key were created, so the attack did change things.

q.title: Lock down a new AWS account
q.scenario: The unit just opened a new AWS account for a training project. You are the first person in it. Build the day-one plan in a sensible order. Some ideas do not belong. Add the steps in the order they should happen.
q.ticket: Request ACCT-31: new training account. Use the root user only to get started.

rules.text: Turn on MFA for the root user
rules.why: The root user can do anything, so it gets a second factor before anything else is built.

rules.text: Set up admin access with IAM Identity Center or a role
rules.why: Named admin identities let people work with least privilege and leave a trail in the logs.

rules.text: Stop signing in as root and use the admin identity
rules.why: Daily work as root is an unneeded risk. Switch only once the admin identity works.

rules.text: Create a CloudTrail trail to keep the API history
rules.why: The default history lasts 90 days. A trail keeps a longer audit record of who did what.
An alert catches a surprise bill early, for example from a forgotten instance.

rules.text: Turn on GuardDuty and review Trusted Advisor security checks
rules.why: Threat detection and account checks give you ongoing visibility once the basics are in place.

rules.text: Create root access keys so scripts can use the account
rules.why: Root access keys should not exist. A leaked key gives unlimited control of the account.

rules.text: Share the admin password with the whole team
rules.why: Shared logins destroy accountability and cannot be tied to a person.

rules.text: Make a test bucket public to check connectivity
rules.why: Public buckets expose data to the Internet. Test with private resources and a role.

before.why: Protect root with MFA before building anything else on the account.
Do not stop using root until the replacement admin access works.
Set up the trail under a named admin identity, not as root.

last.why: Detection and review come after the account has an owner, a trail and a budget. They then have something to watch.

q.title: Place the parts of a two-tier VPC
q.scenario: A unit is building a small web app in one VPC. Visitors reach the app from the Internet. The app servers and the database must not be reachable from the Internet, but the app servers need to download updates. Place each part in the right spot. Three parts in the tray do not belong.
q.ticket: Design review VPC-4. Rules: only the load balancer is public, the database is never public, private servers may start outbound connections only.

slots.label: Spot A
slots.hint: the door that connects the VPC to the Internet

slots.label: Spot B
slots.hint: accepts visitor traffic and passes it to the servers

slots.label: Spot C
slots.hint: lets private servers start outbound connections to the Internet

slots.label: Spot D
slots.hint: runs the application code; no inbound Internet route

slots.label: Spot E
slots.hint: managed relational database for the app's records

devs.name: Internet gateway
devs.why: The Internet gateway connects the VPC to the Internet and is the entry point for public subnets.

devs.name: Application Load Balancer
devs.why: The load balancer sits in the public subnet, takes visitor traffic and forwards it to the private servers.

devs.name: NAT gateway
devs.why: The NAT gateway lives in a public subnet so private servers can reach out for updates without being reachable from outside.

devs.name: EC2 app servers
devs.why: App servers belong in a private subnet, reached only through the load balancer.

devs.name: Amazon RDS database
devs.why: The managed database stays private, and only the app servers can connect to it.

devs.name: Database in a public subnet
devs.why: A public database can be found and attacked from the Internet.

devs.name: Snowball Edge device
devs.why: Snowball Edge is for moving data offline or edge computing. It has no role inside a VPC design like this.

devs.name: Root user access keys on servers
devs.why: Root keys on servers give an attacker full control of the account. Servers should use roles.
